get.description: [native] Liveness, for any caller: `status` (healthy|degraded), and HTTP 503 when PostgreSQL or NATS is down. `engine`, `version`, `peers`, `dependencies` and `addons` are returned ONLY to a caller that presents a credential — they describe the deployment, and an anonymous probe needs the status code, not the inventory.

addons.description: Opt-in subsystem states, keyed by add-on name (`trellion`, `evolve`, `trellion_intel`, …). Built from the gateway's `addons::ADDONS` table, so a new add-on appears here with no schema change — clients must render the keys they receive rather than a fixed list. Three of the four states are emitted today by `addons::health_word`: `enabled`; `disabled`, meaning the operator turned it off, which is NOT a fault; and `unlicensed`, meaning the flag is on but no entitlement grants it, which is also not a fault but needs an action the operator can take (`noo security entitlement install <token>`). The per-add-on reason is deliberately NOT carried here — /health is polled by the compose healthcheck and the host watcher on a short interval, and operator prose on every poll costs bandwidth continuously for something only a human reading a console needs. `unhealthy` (flag on, container missing or down) IS a fault and is specced but NOT YET EMITTED — no arm of `health_word` produces it. Treat any unrecognised value as unknown rather than guessing.

addons_dev.description: Present only when some add-on is vouched for by a temporary development signing key rather than a release key (`noo addons trust-key <name> <pubkey> --dev --expires <dur>`): add-on name to `dev (expires YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC)`. The add-on's `addons.<name>` word stays `enabled`; once the key expires it reads `unhealthy` and the add-on drops out of this map. Absent for an anonymous caller.

post.summary: Rotate refresh token, mint access token
post.description: [native] Reads the HttpOnly refresh cookie (noo_refresh; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/auth), validates and rotates it (single-use; revoked-token replay triggers a defensive revoke of all the user's chains), sets a fresh rotated refresh cookie, and returns a new short-lived access token. Also registered at /auth/refresh.

200.description: New access token issued; a rotated refresh cookie is set via Set-Cookie.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or replayed refresh cookie.

post.summary: Revoke refresh token and clear cookie
post.description: [native] Revokes the presented refresh token (if any) and clears the HttpOnly refresh cookie (noo_refresh; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/auth) via an expiring Set-Cookie. Idempotent. Also registered at /auth/logout.

200.description: Refresh token revoked and cookie cleared.

get.description: [native] GET /.well-known/agent.json — PAI's AgentCard for A2A discovery.

post.description: [native] POST /auth/logout — Revoke the presented refresh cookie + clear it from the browser. Idempotent.
[native] POST /auth/refresh — Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token + a rotated refresh cookie.

get.description: [native] GET /bootstrap/prep — the ROOT host-prep phase, fetched by bootstrap-enroll.sh and run under the operator's one attended sudo. Public for the same reason as `/bootstrap`: it is an inert script from the repo; run by nobody but the operator, on a host that has no credential of any kind yet.

[native] GET /bootstrap/apply — the noo-apply root applier (§7b). It refuses any bundle not signed by the cluster CA, which is why serving the SCRIPT publicly is harmless: the script is the lock, not the key.

[native] GET /bootstrap/ca.crt — the cluster CA CERTIFICATE (public half only). This is the trust anchor a brand-new node needs BEFORE the first signed bundle can verify: noo-apply refuses everything without it, so birth is the one moment it must arrive out-of-band. Serving it publicly discloses nothing (a certificate is public by construction); the node fetches it during token-authenticated enrollment, which is the sanctioned trust-on-first-use ceremony. The PRIVATE key never leaves noo-cli.

[native] GET /bootstrap/prep — the ROOT host-prep phase, fetched by bootstrap-enroll.sh and run under the operator's one attended sudo. Public for the same reason as `/bootstrap`: it is an inert script from the repo; run by nobody but the operator, on a host that has no credential of any kind yet.

[native] GET /bootstrap/fetch — the pull-provisioning fetcher, installed by prep-host.sh as /usr/local/bin/noo-fetch. Public like its siblings: an inert script; the bundle it fetches is ciphertext to anyone without the node's birth key, and noo-apply still verifies the CA signature on the plaintext.

post.description: [native] POST /api/cluster/enroll-tailnet — tailnet-native enrollment. No token, no pins: the tailnet IS the authenticated channel.

get.summary: Serve a CLI release asset (or its .sha256)
get.description: [native] Node-side mirror of the GitHub release asset: `GET /bootstrap/cli/<asset>` returns the binary, `<asset>.sha256` returns `<sha>  <name>`. Read by `noo upgrade` on node role and by noo-apply's cli-binary kind.

post.description: [native] POST /mcp/operator — the OPERATOR MCP door (JSON-RPC over HTTPS). Credential mandatory: an mcp:operator service key bound to an account that holds the admin role (re-checked on every call; mint one with `noo security service-key issue <you>-mcp --scopes mcp:operator --user <admin>`). The shared NOO_MCP_TOKEN bearer, retired,  is refused. Its separate plain-HTTP loopback listener (:3100, path /mcp) was removed in stack-v0.2.40.

get.description: Serves `dist/kiosk.html` from the same UI artifact as the console. PUBLIC, like `/`: a top-level navigation cannot carry an Authorization header and the bundle is not the secret — the page holds nothing until the host launcher injects a kiosk token, and every `/api/*` call it then makes is authenticated. Exact paths only. 404 (with an explanation) when the UI artifact predates the kiosk entry.

get.description: Public discovery for the agent identity exchange. **404 when the `identity` add-on has been switched off** — discovery answers "does this exist", so an install without the add-on advertises nothing. `issuer` is derived from the request `Host` (and `X-Forwarded-Proto`), because a self-hosted controller does not know its own external name. `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` is `noomesh_service_key`, a deliberately non-registered value: the credential is a noomesh service key in the `Authorization` header, which is neither `client_secret_basic` nor `client_secret_post`. `response_types_supported` is empty because there is no authorization endpoint — there is no human to redirect and nothing to consent to.

404.description: The `identity` add-on has been switched off on this install.

get.summary: JSON Web Key Set for exchanged agent tokens
get.description: Proposal 49 phase 3. The public half of the exchange's ES256 signing key, so a third party can verify an agent token without holding anything that could mint one. Public by definition. **404 when the `identity` add-on is off.** With the add-on on but no `NOO_JWT_SIGNING_KEY` configured, returns `{"keys": []}` — a valid JWKS meaning "this issuer publishes none", distinguishable from a misrouted request. Only EXCHANGED tokens are signed asymmetrically; dashboard and CLI logins stay HS256, so there is no dual-accept window on the login path. The gateway selects its verification key from the token's own `alg` and pins validation to that one algorithm, which closes algorithm confusion (an HS256 token signed with the published key as the HMAC secret does not verify).

404.description: The `identity` add-on has been switched off on this install.

OperationHandle.description: What an operation-backed route answers 202 with when the run outlasted its wait, and what POST /api/v1/ops answers. Poll `poll` (GET, optionally `?wait=<s>`, at most 25).

joined.description: Present and true when this request joined the same account's run already in flight (exclusive types) and started nothing new.

Operation.description: One asynchronous operation as GET /api/v1/ops/{id} shows it. `result` and `result_status` appear once it has finished; a listing omits them.

params.description: As stored: ingest text is omitted, over-large params replaced by a marker.

result.description: The route's own body, in its own shape.

result_status.description: The HTTP status the synchronous route would have answered.

cancel.description: Present on a cancelled op: {gateway_aborted, worker_stopped, note}. `worker_stopped` is false: a worker run already underway is not stopped.

retry_safe.description: On a failed op: whether resubmitting is harmless.
